extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and peer reviewers (R21/R33 Microbicide Innovation Program), research investigators preparing/responding to NIAID review
extracted.subtask_description: Summary statement and critique from an NIAID Special Emphasis Panel describing the evaluation criteria and reviewer guidance used to assess an R21/R33 application (microbicide research). Useful for applicants preparing NIH grant applications and for reviewers performing peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Priority Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact/Priority score assigned after discussion (reported here as 30 for this application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion of an application by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by the individual reviewers and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? Strengths and weaknesses relating to the scientific importance of the proposed work are enumerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers list strengths (e.g., novel target, potential for synergy with other microbicides, encouraging preliminary data) and weaknesses (e.g., limited literature supporting in vivo relevance of SEVI, potential over-ambitious scope).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited, trained, and capable of carrying out the work? Reviewers evaluate qualifications, complementarity, and history of collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths include complementary expertise, history of collaboration, and inclusion of appropriate subcontract/company. Weaknesses are noted if any (none in many reviewer comments here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms? Are novel concepts, approaches, methodologies or interventions proposed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation includes whether targeting a non-viral host factor (SEVI) is novel and whether using amyloid-binding molecules repurposed from Alzheimer’s research is innovative; weaknesses include use of standard toxicity models which may not be innovative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the study design, methods, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the aims? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success considered?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess logical progression, balance of efficacy and toxicity testing, appropriateness of models (cell lines, explants, rabbit vaginal irritation), clarity of go/no-go decision points, feasibility within proposed time, and potential gaps (e.g., limited tissue types tested, insufficient justification for excluding X4 isolates, details on screening metrics and hit rates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment contribute to the probability of success? Are institutional support, equipment, and other resources adequate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths include institutional commitment to women’s health, adequate space and facilities, and strong statistical support. Weaknesses noted when appropriate (none here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestones / Go-No-Go Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative milestones and decision points that determine progression from R21 to R33 phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Milestones should be well presented, quantifiable, and provide clear go/no-go decisions. Reviewers praised well-defined milestones here but noted that some goals might be set low or that breadth of some aims could complicate analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of protections for human subjects involved in the research (certification codes provided: e.g., 30 - Human subjects involved - Certified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers judge whether descriptions of human subject involvement are adequate. This application: 'PROTECTION OF HUMAN SUBJECTS (Resume): ACCEPTABLE (Code 30)'. Any SRG concerns would be reported; none were noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Plans (Women, Minorities, Children)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for inclusion of women, minorities, and children in the research, with NIH enrollment category codes reported (e.g., G3A, M1A, C1A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether inclusion plans are scientifically acceptable. Example notes: 'INCLUSION OF WOMEN PLAN (Resume): ACCEPTABLE (G3A) - No women are involved because the human subject involvement consists of semen collection.' 'INCLUSION OF MINORITIES PLAN (Resume): ACCEPTABLE (M1A)'; 'INCLUSION OF CHILDREN PLAN (Resume): ACCEPTABLE (C1A)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animal Protections / Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of vertebrate animal involvement and protections (e.g., '30 - Vertebrate animals involved - no SRG concerns noted'; 'Vertebrate Animals (Resume): ACCEPTABLE (Code 30)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note appropriateness of animal models (e.g., rabbit vaginal irritation model), IACUC status (approval pending noted), and recommend refinement if necessary to satisfy animal care committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of biosafety and whether facilities and policies are adequate for proposed biohazard work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated here as 'ACCEPTABLE' with the note that adequate facilities and policies are described for work with biohazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated 'ACCEPTABLE' in this review; reviewers expect appropriate sharing or explanation when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Budgetary Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of budget justification, appropriateness of personnel and costs, and committee budget recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative note: the budget shown is the requested budget and may be adjusted by grants management if an award is planned. Committee here 'recommended the budget as requested' but also commented that personnel and costs may be more substantial than some aspects of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion Scoring Process / Calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural description of how criterion scores and overall impact score are handled in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion scores (Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment) are submitted by assigned reviewers prior to the meeting. These criterion scores are not discussed at the meeting and are not calculated into the overall impact score during the discussion; the overall impact score is based on reviewers' overall scores after discussion and is averaged and multiplied by 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths and Weaknesses Narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide bulleted 'Strengths' and 'Weaknesses' under each scored criterion to justify ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative detail should identify specific methodological or conceptual strengths (e.g., complementary expertise, strong preliminary data) and weaknesses (e.g., limited in vivo relevance, overly broad aims, inadequate model selection). These narratives inform applicants how to revise proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility / Scope Concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the proposed scope is realistic and whether aims might be too broad to be completed as proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers comment on feasibility (e.g., 'scope may be a bit optimistic', 'Aim 3 is complex and could have been two aims'), and may advise narrowing or clarifying synthesis/screening plans, predicted hit rates, and sample sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model and Assay Appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the biological models and assays used for efficacy and toxicity testing (cell lines, explants, in vivo models).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess representativeness (e.g., A2En and SiHa cells may not represent vaginal tissue), diversity of explant surfaces to test, relevance of commensal bacteria assays (concerns over using MRS broth), and recommend additional models (e.g., animal models to assess in vivo SEVI relevance).
